steps.title: Prepare ECG miniature connector
steps.instruction: Fix a circular miniature connector (6 pins) in a third‑hand clamp, bend the five peripheral pins to 90°, pinch the central pin with fine forceps and twist it off at the base; optionally remove or bend the unused pins for extra support.

steps.title: Solder electrode wires to connector
steps.instruction: Cut two pieces of stainless‑steel 7‑strand wire to 7 cm, strip 5 mm from one end, place a tiny drop of orthophosphoric acid on pins #1 and #2, align stripped ends onto the pins, briefly melt a small amount of soldering tin onto each pin/wire pair (do not overheat the pin), and repeat for both pins.

steps.title: Solder reference wire
steps.instruction: Cut a reference wire to 2 cm, strip its end, apply a drop of orthophosphoric acid to connector pin #6, solder the wire onto pin #6 using the same brief soldering technique as above.

steps.title: Test solder joints and apply glue
steps.instruction: Pull each soldered wire quickly to confirm a strong joint; apply a thin layer of transparent glue (Silisto) to all connections and stripped wire parts, then fit the matching female connector onto the male connector to check fit.

steps.title: Verify connector continuity
steps.instruction: Strip the very tip of each electrode wire, use fine tools and a multimeter in resistance mode to probe each female‑connector pin; only the correct pin should show low resistance, confirming no short circuits.

steps.title: Assemble headstage side of patch cable
steps.instruction: Cut an ultra‑flexible microminiature shielded cable of sufficient length (long enough to allow loops during recordings). Slide the M9 connector casing onto the cable, then sequentially add heat‑shrink tubes (large, intermediate, small). Remove ~1 cm of insulation, gently unbraid the sheath with a blunt needle, bundle the sheath loosely, unwind individual wires, strip 1–2 mm of each wire, dip briefly in orthophosphoric acid, and solder each wire onto pins #1, #2, and the grounding pin of the connector, using minimal acid and avoiding overheating. Align the cable end over the pins with a third‑hand tool, apply a tiny acid drop to each pin before soldering, and after soldering apply glue in stages from bottom to top of the pins, curing each layer with Paladur solvent. Add tension to the cable (e.g., gentle pull and a small weight) to keep it taut. Slide the smallest heat‑shrink tube over the glued area, then the intermediate and large tubes, heating each briefly without melting the thin wire insulation. Prepare a 1 cm piece of regular wire for grounding: de‑insulate ~1 cm, coat with solder, insert into the smallest heat‑shrink tube together with the cable, apply acid and solder to the sheath, slide the tube down to the glue, and heat‑shrink carefully.

steps.title: Assemble mouse side of patch cable
steps.instruction: Slide two heat‑shrink tubes (one slightly larger than the connector, one loose) onto the cable end. Secure the miniature connector in a crocodile clamp, bend its pins outward, place the cable on top, and solder each wire to its designated pin, keeping solder joints thin and shiny; return pins to straight position. Embed the soldered area in transparent glue, then wrap at least two layers of Teflon tape around the glue (apply a thin film of super‑glue to the cured glue before Teflon to prevent shifting). Cut a piece of aluminum foil matching the distance from connector bottom to stripped cable, glue it over the glue‑covered area, trim excess, and spread the cable sheath over the foil. Slide the tightest heat‑shrink tube over the assembly and shrink it, then repeat with the larger tube, keeping the assembly straight. Verify continuity with a multimeter, ensuring each pin connects only to its counterpart.

steps.title: Prepare animal and anesthesia
steps.instruction: Weigh the mouse, inject buprenorphine 0.1 mg kg⁻¹ subcutaneously in the neck 20–30 min before surgery. Induce anesthesia in an isoflurane chamber at 4 % isoflurane with 0.6 L min⁻¹ oxygen flow, then transfer to a heating pad and maintain at 1.5 % isoflurane via a mask, confirming deep anesthesia by lack of paw reflex. Apply depilatory cream (Veet) to a 1 × 1 cm area on the head and to the upper right and lower left chest, then rinse. Disinfect skin three times with Cutasept, and inject 200 µL of Naropin subcutaneously under the scalp for local anesthesia.

steps.title: Create skin incisions and insert cannula
steps.instruction: Using sharp scissors, excise a 0.5 × 0.5 cm patch of skin on the head. Turn the mouse supine, disinfect the chest skin three times with Cutasept, and make a 3–5 mm incision on the chest. Insert a feeding cannula (30 G) subcutaneously from the chest incision toward the head incision, keeping the tip facing outward; keep the cannula in sterile water before insertion and sterilize after use.

steps.title: Thread ECG wire through cannula
steps.instruction: Pass the ECG wire from the connector through the hollow feeding cannula from the head side; when the wire emerges at the chest opening, gently pull the cannula out, leaving the wire in place. If tissue blocks the cannula, poke the obstruction with a needle to clear it, then sterilize the cannula again.

steps.title: Prepare wire tip with glue
steps.instruction: Strip 5 mm from the wire tip with fine forceps, apply a small amount of viscous glue (Pattex) to the stripped end (do not spread excessively), and polymerize the glue with a few drops of Paladur solvent. Optionally flatten the tip between forceps to spread strands for better glue adhesion.

steps.title: Suture wire to muscle and close skin
steps.instruction: Dissect connective tissue to expose underlying muscle, then suture the glued wire onto the muscle perpendicular to the fibers with a knot placed close to the glue. Leave enough wire length to avoid impeding locomotion; a small loop can be left subcutaneously on the head side. Close the chest skin with two interrupted sutures, disinfect the wound with an iodine‑based disinfectant (Braunol). Repeat the same procedure on the opposite chest side with the second wire.

steps.title: Implant connector on skull
steps.instruction: Turn the mouse prone, remove remaining tissue from the skull with a cotton bud, and roughen the skull surface gently with the back of a scalpel blade. Ensure the skull is completely dry, then glue the miniature connector onto the skull using transparent glue, polymerizing with Paladur solvent. Slide a short stripped portion of the remaining wire subcutaneously and glue it onto the bone. Form a head cap by adding more glue around the connector and curing it, then apply an opaque black glue layer over the cap. Verify that enough skull surface is exposed for a solid cap.

steps.title: Post‑operative care and monitoring
steps.instruction: Inject metacam 2 mg kg⁻¹ subcutaneously, place the mouse in its cage under an infrared lamp, and monitor until fully recovered from anesthesia (typically ~1 h). Check recovery every 12 h for 7 days, then monitor weight and general state daily; pay close attention to suture integrity. Animals usually regain pre‑surgery weight after 3–4 days.

steps.title: Optional head‑cap removal
steps.instruction: At experiment end, place the head cap in acetone overnight (≤12 h) to dissolve the cyanoacrylate glue; then rinse with water and dry. Check pin integrity and overall condition; reuse connectors only after confirming each pin connects correctly with a female connector. Change acetone if it becomes saturated, and avoid prolonged exposure to prevent connector damage.

steps.title: Habituate animal to handling
steps.instruction: Allow the mouse to recover for at least one week before recordings. Handle the animal for a minimum of three days: let it explore the palm of the hand, then gradually habituate it to being held by gently gripping the head cap with the index finger and thumb while securing the tail with the other fingers.

steps.title: Connect cable and set recording parameters
steps.instruction: On recording day, connect the mouse’s head cap to the patch cable, secure the cable with a pulley system (two grooved wheels, lightweight thread, and a 5 mL syringe as counterweight), and adjust the counterweight by changing the water level in the syringe. Tie the thread to the cable and syringe head, positioning the knot empirically. Turn on the amplifier only when the cable is connected. Set the acquisition sampling rate to ≥5 kHz. Configure amplifier filters: low‑pass around 1 kHz, high‑pass 30 Hz, and enable a 50 Hz (or 60 Hz) notch filter if needed. Adjust gain so the ECG signal is clearly visible without saturation, and set offset so the baseline sits near the middle of the acquisition range (≈0 V for a –5 V to +5 V system).

steps.title: Synchronize video and ECG acquisition
steps.instruction: Plan synchronization before the experiment; ensure the ECG acquisition system and video recording system start simultaneously or use a common trigger. Verify that both clocks run at the same rate to avoid drift; if necessary, record timestamps from both systems for post‑hoc alignment.

description:
Validation of protocol This protocol or parts of it has been used and validated in the following research
article: Signoret-Genest et al. (2023). Integrated cardio-behavioral responses to threat
define defensive states. Nature Neuroscience (all figures). We are providing a small data set along with the current protocol, allowing to access
examples of raw ECG data as well as the corresponding pre-processing and analysis
procedures. Additionally, we provide open-access code that can be applied to any
steps for testing and experimentation.
